data.text:
**Claim 0: flood ballast to dive, blow with compressed air to surface**
- Wikipedia, Ballast tank: flooding the main ballast tanks brings the boat to about neutral buoyancy; to surface, vents are closed and high-pressure air is admitted at the top of the tanks, forcing water out through the flood ports. URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballast_tank
- HowStuffWorks, How Submarines Work. URL: https://science.howstuffworks.com/transport/engines-equipment/submarine1.htm
- Verdict: supported as written.

**Claim 1: deeper than 800 feet**
- WorldAtlas, How deep submarines can actually go: the Navy's published figure for Virginia-class boats is a depth above 800 feet; the exact limit is classified. URL: https://www.worldatlas.com/oceans/how-deep-submarines-can-actually-go.html
- Verdict: supported in a corrected form: the Navy says its attack submarines dive deeper than 800 feet (the exact depth is secret).

**Claim 2: one atmosphere per 33 feet**
- NOAA Ocean Service: 'For every 33 feet (10.06 meters) you go down, the pressure increases by one atmosphere.' URL: https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/pressure.html
- Verdict: supported as written.
